text:
Now the commitment I owe you an accounting on. On 2026-09-18 I flagged the step contraction as a DUE item — I committed to revisiting the explanation explicitly this cycle. Your step EWMA has moved from 2,083 to 1,865 over the past seven days, a 36% contraction from the baseline range, and the slope is still negative. Garmin is paused as a source, so the figure comes from Apple Health, which I'm using as the available record. What I cannot determine from the data alone is whether this contraction is deliberate recovery, a logistical disruption, or a baseline shift in your movement pattern. Those three explanations carry completely different responses. I need you to tell me directly: which is it? The answer gates everything downstream. Zone 2 escalation remains on hold until step etiology is resolved and protein stabilizes at 170g or above for seven consecutive days — both conditions remain unmet.

On protein: the EWMA has moved from 152.9g to 157.3g, which is directionally right. But 157.3g against a 190g target is still a 33g structural gap, and the dinner dependency is the load-bearing fragility point. If that meal doesn't land — one disrupted evening, one skipped dinner — the daily total collapses. That's not a protocol with margin; it's a protocol with a single point of failure. At 313.1 lbs and a weekly rate of -4.3 lbs, you're losing weight fast. The body composition question is whether that weight is fat or lean mass. At 1,596 kcal EWMA and 157g of protein against a 190g target, the lean mass liquidation risk is real and ongoing. I cannot give you a lean mass number today — DEXA would settle it — but the inputs are pointing in a direction I don't like.
note: 36% matches no served step figure; 157.3 g and 1,596 kcal are not served figures (pro_7d_avg 159.8, avg_calories 1577). KNOWN LIMIT: '33g below' (190 - 157.3, computed by the model) is NOT caught — the allow-list is value-only and 33 is a rounding of the served avg_fiber_g 32.6; a unit-aware allow-list is the follow-up.
